author: claude
description: Offset pagination on `GET /api/orders` skips and repeats rows when new orders arrive while a merchant scrolls, and deep offsets are slow on large accounts. This switches the endpoint to opaque keyset cursors: each page returns `nextCursor`, the client passes it back as `?cursor=`, and the DB layer gains a `createdBefore` filter. The cursor also carries the status filter from the first request so later pages stay consistent if the client drops the query string. `offset` is removed from the public params. Tests cover walking all pages, keeping the filter, and rejecting a malformed cursor.

defects.mechanism: The cursor position records only createdAt and the query uses a strict createdAt < filter, but createdAt is whole seconds and the DB orders ties by id. When a page boundary falls inside a group of orders created in the same second, the rest of that group is never returned.

When a cursor is present, the query scope (including accountId) is taken from the client-supplied cursor instead of the session's accountId. The cursor is unsigned base64 JSON, so any merchant can edit it, or replay one from another account, to list another account's orders.

The rewrite replaced the single batched `customers.getMany` per page with one `customers.get` per order. Each call is an HTTP round trip to the CRM, so a 100-row page now makes 100 requests instead of one.
